cards.explanation: The answer is a great conflict. The message was true, and it concerned a great conflict (Daniel 10:1). Daniel, also called Belteshazzar, doesn't get a pleasant little forecast here, friends. The understanding of it was given to him in a vision.

The answer is True. Daniel says, "I ate no rich food, no meat or wine entered my mouth…" (Daniel 10:3). He also didn't anoint himself with oil until the three weeks were completed. That's a long stretch without anything fancy on the plate, bakers.

The answer is the Tigris. Daniel was standing on the bank of the great river, the Tigris (Daniel 10:4). It was the twenty-fourth day of the first month, friends. That's where he lifted up his eyes and saw a certain man dressed in linen.

The answer is False. Daniel describes his body as "like beryl." His face was "…like the brilliance of lightning…" and his eyes "…like flaming torches…" (Daniel 10:6). His voice was "…like the sound of a multitude." Nothing ordinary about that, bakers.

The answer is that they run and hide themselves. The men with Daniel didn't see the vision, but a great terror fell on them, and they ran and hid themselves (Daniel 10:7). Only Daniel saw the vision, and the rest took off. I'd like to say I'd stay put, friends, but I'd be right behind them.

The answer is that none of it remains. Daniel says, "No strength remained in me; my face grew deathly pale, and I was powerless." (Daniel 10:8). He was left alone gazing at this great vision. I think anybody would feel their knees quit, bakers.

The answer is False. Daniel does not stay standing on the riverbank. He says, "I heard the sound of his words, and as I listened, I fell into a deep sleep, with my face to the ground." (Daniel 10:9). He went down, not up, friends. The riverbank got a front row view of Daniel's face.

The answer is that he has now been sent to Daniel. The one speaking says, "Stand up, for I have now been sent to you." (Daniel 10:11). He also tells Daniel to consider carefully the words he's about to say. So the reason for standing up, bakers, is that he has been sent to Daniel.
The answer is True. Daniel says, "And when he had said this to me, I stood up trembling." (Daniel 10:11). He was shaking, but he got up. Standing on shaky legs still counts, friends.

The answer is True. The one sent to Daniel says, "…from the first day that you purposed to understand and to humble yourself before your God, your words were heard, and I have come in response to them." (Daniel 10:12). Daniel's words were heard. That's a good thing to hold onto, bakers.

The answer is the prince of the kingdom of Persia. The one sent to Daniel says, "…the prince of the kingdom of Persia opposed me for twenty-one days." (Daniel 10:13). That's why he showed up after Daniel's words were already heard from the first day, friends. The text says this prince opposed him, and it says no more about who he is.

The answer is Michael. The one sent to Daniel says, "Then Michael, one of the chief princes, came to help me…" (Daniel 10:13). Twenty-one days of opposition, and then help shows up. I'd call that good news, bakers.

The answer is what will happen to Daniel's people in the latter days. The one sent to Daniel says, "Now I have come to explain to you what will happen to your people in the latter days, for the vision concerns those days." (Daniel 10:14). That's the whole reason for this visit, friends. It's about Daniel's people and what's ahead.

The answer is that he becomes speechless. Daniel says, "…I set my face toward the ground and became speechless." (Daniel 10:15). That's a lot to take in, and he went quiet. I think I'd go quiet too, bakers.

The answer is True. Daniel says, "…one with the likeness of a man touched my lips, and I opened my mouth and said…" (Daniel 10:16). Speechless one moment, talking the next. Daniel found his voice, friends.

The answer is False. The one with the likeness of a man does not leave Daniel to recover on his own. Daniel says, "Again the one with the likeness of a man touched me and strengthened me." (Daniel 10:18). I think that's a kind thing to see in the middle of such a scary scene, bakers.

The answer is that Daniel says to speak because he has been strengthened. Daniel says, "Speak, my lord, for you have strengthened me." (Daniel 10:19). He had said he had no breath left, and now he's ready to listen. Quite a turnaround, friends.

The answer is to fight against the prince of Persia. The one speaking with Daniel says, "I must return at once to fight against the prince of Persia…" (Daniel 10:20). So he has more work waiting, bakers. He also says that when he has gone forth, the prince of Greece will come.

The answer is what is inscribed in the Book of Truth. The one speaking with Daniel says, "But first I will tell you what is inscribed in the Book of Truth." (Daniel 10:21). He has a fight waiting, and he still stops to tell Daniel this first, friends. Whatever is in that book, it comes before he goes.
